event_description: By Richard Maltby and David Shire Directed by Bruce Miller Closer Than Ever is a an intimate musical revue. While the songs do not follow a particular plot, they are related in theme in that they each tell a story about relationships, family, and friendship. The musical is not a holiday show but the often humorous lyrics are very uplifting and perfect for a cozy winter evening. They're about love, friendship, security, and happiness - holding onto those essentials in a world that seems to spin faster every day. In 1989, the New York Times described it as "one of the half-dozen finest American theater scores of the last decade.” This Off Broadway classic originally opened with a smash hit production in Greenwich Village in 1989, and was most recently revived in NYC this season, once again earning universal raves from critics and audiences alike. That recent hit revival closed recently after a sold-out five month run.

event_description: A performance by the Cashore Marionettes is a celebration of life. The program consists of a collection of engaging pieces encompassing a broad range of themes, each delivered with a simplicity that expresses the essence of the moment. This world-renowned marionette company will entertain audiences of all ages. Visit cashoremarionettes.com for a sneak peek at this amazing art form. Two Separate Productions: Choose Your Favorite, or Enjoy Both! Life in Motion This performance is a series of scenes taken from everyday life and set to beautiful music by composers such as Beethoven, Vivaldi, Strauss, and Copland. Through a combination of virtuoso manipulation, humor, pathos, classic music, and poetic insight, The Cashore Marionettes take the audience on a journey that celebrates the richness of life. Life in Motion is a powerful, entertaining, surprising, one-of-a-kind evening for adults and young adults. Simple Gifts Simple Gifts is also a series of scenes from everyday life set to stunning music by Vivaldi, Strauss, Beethoven and Copland. Through a combination of virtuoso manipulation, beautiful music, theatrical illusion, and artistic insight, the original vignettes presented in Simple Gifts provide an entertaining and sensitive vision of what it is to be human. The marionettes are engineering marvels and the quality of movement is extraordinary. Adults, younger children, and young adults will all enjoy the range of emotions with characters and actions that are amazingly convincing.

event_description: From Friday, October 31 – Sunday, November 2, special 20-minute tours leave every half hour (on the hour and half hour) from 5:00-9:00 p.m., with the last boat departing at 8:30 p.m. This year’s tours plunge passengers into a chilling adventure to investigate reported strange and monstrous occurrences along Richmond’s riverfront. Passengers will be deputized by our brave boat captains to find a mysterious monster that has been plaguing Richmond’s riverfront. Guests will venture downstream on the historic James River and Kanawha Canal and witness the spooky décor and chilling surprises as they face the aquatic peril that lurks just below the surface. We hope that with your help the monster will be kept at bay. Do you dare venture forth into dark waters guided only by dim lamplight? Little ghouls and ghosts in attendance will receive a special candy treat. This Eerie Canal Tour is best suited for kids aged 7 and over. Boats depart from the Canal Walk’s Turning Basin at 139 Virginia Street. Admission is $6. Kids aged 4 and under are free.

event_description: Discover Richmond from a whole new perspective on this fun, interactive 45-minute tour! Join a Valentine guide as you journey through the city’s past, explore Richmond’s role in local, state, and federal government, and soak in spectacular panoramic views from the 18th-floor Observation Deck at City Hall. Along the way, you’ll help shape the experience by choosing which Richmond stories you’d like to hear, making every tour different. Wrap up your visit with a nostalgic look at Broad Street through vintage ViewMasters featuring historic images from the Valentine’s collection. Whether you’re a first-time visitor, a longtime local, or just short on time, this tour is the perfect way to experience the people, places and moments that have made Richmond.

event_description: Haunted Capitol Hill Ghost Tour by Haunts of Richmond Rising above the city, Capitol Hill has long been the seat of power in Richmond, Virginia, but many believe it is also watched over by something far older and far less visible. On this Richmond ghost tour, join Haunts of Richmond for an evening walk through the historic heart of the Commonwealth. Guided through the grounds of Capitol Square and surrounding streets, guests will hear chilling stories rooted in Virginia’s political past, tragic events, and decades of reported paranormal encounters. Tales include accounts connected to the Haunted Executive Mansion, lingering spirits said to roam Capitol Square, and the devastating Great Theatre Fire, one of the deadliest disasters in Richmond’s history. Blending history with eerie folklore and firsthand reports, this atmospheric walking ghost tour explores why Capitol Hill remains one of Richmond’s most quietly haunted districts, where politics rules the day, but shadows claim the night. Join Haunts of Richmond and ascend Capitol Hill for an unforgettable evening of haunted history. For tour details and additional information, please drop us a note or check out the Haunts of Richmond website.

event_description: Ladies leave your man at home! Earlybirds Club is a dance party designed for women and gender-expansive folks that starts at 6pm and ends at 10pm - because we have stuff to do in the morning! 80s, 90s, and 2000s pop, hip-hop, new wave, and R&B A judgment-free dance floor built on joy, kindness, and connection Doors at 6pm, done by 10pm Come solo, come with friends, come ready to sweat. Note: While Earlybirds Club does not police identity at the door, they ask that everyone who purchases a ticket respects this as a safe space for women and gender-expansive folks. Earlybirds Club is a dance party designed for women, trans, and non-binary folks that starts at 6pm and ends at 10pm—because we have shit to do in the morning! DJ Helean spins music from the 80s to 2000s, including pop, hip-hop, new wave, and R&B—you know, the songs you sing at the top of your lungs when no one's home! Earlybirds Club is more than a fun night out, it's a supportive space where kindness, good vibes, and sensible footwear rule, and 10% of proceeds always benefit a local non-profit. Come as you are—there’s plenty of room on the dance floor for everyone.

event_description: "Gallery5 is partnering with the Richmond Moon Market for First Friday, Richmond’s premier event celebrating the arts! This annual Richmond tradition is the proper kickoff to Autumn and Halloween/Samhain "spooky season". Join at Gallery5 from 5-11pm for Richmond Arts District's RVA First Fridays in Historic Jackson Ward for a night of visual and performing art, live music, DJs, circus arts, belly dancing, tarot reading, vendors, and YOU! Party Liberation Foundation (PLF) will be joining outside for a fire performance-filled Pyro Circus complete with DJs and special acts. Richmond Moon Market will have two blocks of local maker vendor tents! We strongly encourage everyone to dress up in whatever costuming and creative attire that you so desire! Be sure to get there early to catch all the wicked goodness! RVA First Fridays is always a FREE community event! THANK YOU AND WELCOME TO THE SHOW!

event_description: The 2nd Street Festival will return this fall, Saturday-Sunday, October 3-4! The festival celebrates the rich culture of the historic Jackson Ward neighborhood in Downtown Richmond, VA. This FREE event is produced by Venture Richmond Events. Each year thousands visit historic Jackson Ward to reminisce about the days when 2nd Street was the heart and soul of Richmond's African American community and was known as “the Harlem of the South.” Today, Jackson Ward continues to be a thriving neighborhood and community. The 2nd Street Festival is an annual celebration over two days that features three stages of live musical entertainment along with a Kidz Zone, popular food vendors, a marketplace and Artists Row to shop, and the Richmond Metropolitan Antique Car Club. Find all event information here!

event_name: Bo Johnson Stand Up Comedy Show
event_description: Stand-up comedian Bo Johnson (Comedy Central, Don't Tell Comedy) comes to Coalition Theater! Bo Johnson is a comedian from Seattle, Washington. He can be found headlining clubs, breweries, and appropriately sized theaters across the United States and Canada. His stand up has been featured on Netflix is a Joke Radio, season two of Kevin Hart Presents: Hart of the City on Comedy Central, Don’t Tell Comedy Secret Sets (twice), Hulu, & LOL Live! at the prestigious Just For Laughs comedy festival in Montreal. He was a finalist in the 39th annual Seattle International Comedy Competition and is a regular at festivals including Bumbershoot, SF Sketchfest, the Double Down Comedy Experience sponsored by Zappos, Life is Beautiful in Las Vegas, Rifflandia in Victoria BC, Prizefest, and Big Pine Comedy Festival in Phoenix. Bo has opened for major acts including Marc Maron, Joe Dombrowski, Jessica Kirson, and David Nihill. With a growing online audience Bo’s jokes have been viewed millions of times online. Most recently he released his first full length special, “Two Sailboats” in 2025. Deadline included Bo in their Future of Funny list and regarding his special wrote, “For my money, Bo Johnson had one of the best debut specials in recent memory in Two Sailboats , a self-released hour culminating in a joke performed by his father…”

event_description: The American Civil War Museum is pleased to announce the Annual Lincoln Prize Lecture will be held at the Tredegar site in Richmond, Virginia on October 15th, 2026. This event is in partnership with Gilder Lehrman Institute for American History. Our partnership with Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History is reflective of our continuing commitment to engage in national conversations about the Civil War by presenting the most respected authorities in the field of research and scholarship. The Gilder Lehrman annual Lincoln Prize award is given to the finest scholarly work in English on Abraham Lincoln, the American Civil War soldier, or the American Civil War era. This year’s recipient is Dr. Richard Carwardine, Distinguished Fellow of the Rothermere American Institute at Oxford, for his book Righteous Strife: How Warring Religious Nationalists Forged Lincoln’s Union. A two-time recipient of the Gilder Lehrman Lincoln Prize, Dr. Carwardine is a Welsh-born historian of the United States. He spent over thirty years in the Department of History at Sheffield University before taking up the Rhodes Professorship of American History at Oxford in 2002. He was elected President of Corpus Christi College, Oxford in 2009 and navigated the College towards the 500th anniversary of its founding. He received his first Lincoln Prize in 2004 for his book Lincoln: A Life of Purpose and Power. The ACWM Lincoln Prize Lecture includes a reception with Dr. Carwardine followed by the lecture and book signing in the Museum.

event_name: A Spooky Night at the (Poe) Museum with Lisa Perrin and Malorie Mackey
event_description: It's not spooky season without a visit to some of Richmond's haunted places! Lisa and Malorie will be talking with Kelly (and maybe some spirits?) at the Poe Museum. Both books will be available for purchase and signing! About the Books: A gorgeous and delightfully spooky compendium of famous (and infamous) spiritual mediums from around the world and across the centuries who have claimed to communicate with the dead. With a particular emphasis on the Spiritualism craze of the late 19th and early 20th century, The Secrets of the Séance Society spotlights these larger-than-life characters who shared their gifts privately with clients and often found their way onto stages and into newspaper headlines. The book also highlights famous fraudsters and the tenacious investigators who debunked them. With respectful sincerity and a healthy dose of humor, bestselling author/illustrator Lisa Perrin weaves together these stories, ultimately exploring the deeper question of why the living world is endlessly trying to connect with the dead. Whether you’re a determined skeptic or a true believer, you’ll enjoy this thrilling and irreverent history of mediums and their fabulous history. From Malorie Mackey—adventurer, explorer, writer, and host of the Amazon Prime travel show Weird World Adventures—here is a photo-rich guide to over 500 of the most haunting, mysterious, uncanny, and gloriously goth destinations around the globe. Finding inspiration in everything from ancient mythology to Victorian mourning traditions, classic horror movies, and beyond, The Goth Atlas will help you plan your trip to sites like: Caerphilly Castle in Wales and Himeji Castle in Japan, both famously populated by spirits; Abandoned and haunted edifices, including Philadelphia's fortress-like Eastern State Penitentiary, where Al Capone was once incarcerated; Museums and monuments celebrating global death rituals, such as the Museum of Anthropology's Room of 10,000 Ancient Skulls in Lima, Peru; Eerie art installations, including Mexico City’s disquieting Island of the Dolls; plus Alternative music festivals, clubs, shopping districts, witch markets, and more. About the Authors: Lisa Perrin is an award-winning illustrator, designer, entrepreneur, and educator. She is a professor in the illustration department at MICA, and her work has been recognized by The Society of Illustrators, American Illustration, 3X3 magazine, and PRINT magazine. Perrin can often be found obsessively artmaking and imbuing her life with unfettered whimsy. Her work explores the old world in a new way, combining humor with darkness and beauty with strangeness. Perrin’s first book, The League of Lady Poisoners, was published in 2023. She lives in Baltimore, MD. https://www.madebyperrin.com/ Malorie Mackey is a host, adventurer, professional explorer, and full-time writer-editor, with a focus on travel, adventure, the paranormal, and the macabre. She created and runs her own travel and adventure blog, MaloriesAdventures.com, where she showcases the world’s most unusual locations. Malorie’s work has helped bring her unique travel show, Weird World Adventures, on Amazon Prime to life, showcasing exciting adventures through the most bizarre and haunted places in the United States.

event_name: Emoween: A Still Not Okay Tour (Tribute to My Chemical Romance, Paramore, The All American Rejects)
event_description: EMOWEEN featuring tributes to My Chemical Romance, Paramore, The All American Rejects! The Still Not Okay Tour brings the energy, emotion, and anthems of the 2000s emo and pop-punk era back to the stage with three powerhouse tribute acts: Forever This Way performing as My Chemical Romance, delivering The Black Parade in its entirety; Fake Happy, capturing the raw intensity of Paramore’s formative years; and The Dirty Little Rejects, a high-energy tribute to The All-American Rejects. In addition to the touring tributes, the show will also feature an up and coming band from each city it visits! Packed with nostalgia, high production value, and the full-band sound that defined a generation, the Still Not Okay Tour offers fans a chance to relive the songs, community, and cathartic release of the era… live, loud, and exactly how they remember it.

event_name: 4th Friday Art Shows and Opening Reception at Art Works!
event_description: Join on October 23rd, 2026, from 6–8 p.m. for the exciting opening reception of our new exhibits at Art Works. Meet the talented artists, enjoy live music, refreshments, and libations sponsored by RVA Thriving Artists, and celebrate another vibrant season of creativity and community. Embrace the Halloween spirit by dressing up in your favorite costume and join us for an unforgettable evening as we unveil our latest art exhibits. Immerse yourself works by Sky Dai, Johnye Bennett, Lew Lott, Carol Gruppé and Unmask curated by Susan Vaughan. The All Media Show features art by local artists. The Bridge Project will continue exhibiting Nathan Hosmer Nevarez until November 30th. Don’t miss out on this night of art and enchantment! This event is free and open to the public, with convenient, free parking available. Exhibits will remain on view through November 14th, 2026 (unless otherwise noted). Carol Gruppé will remain up until October 31st. Also see 80+ working artist studios.

event_name: Do The Halloween Pub Crawl in Richmond!
event_description: Get ready to embrace the spooky season and Do The Halloween Pub Crawl in Downtown Richmond! Pull out your spookiest costumes, grab your ghoulish friends, and prepare for a night of haunted fun. It's the most frightfully fantastic pub crawl, where the spirits are high, and the fun never dies! With contests, prizes, and downtown fun, this is the Halloween Pub Crawl event you should do. Come solo, with your boo, or gather your whole ghoul-gang and join for the spookiest Halloween bash! Pub crawl stops include: Poe’s Pub McCormack’s Irish Pub Rosie Connolly’s Pub Restaurant And food stops include: La Bodega Latin Kitchen & Cocktails RVA Bottoms Up Pizza and more! What to expect at the Do The Halloween Pub Crawl: Express Check-in: Skip the line and check yourself in when you arrive-no waiting, no hassle, just pure party power. Your night of patriotic fun starts whenever you do! (Note: This check-in is for the event entrance, not individual recommended stops.) Social media challenges: Say Cheers! Largest Group PIC on the ‘gram Snap and post a creepy, kooky, or just plain killer group photo with your costumed crew, or anyone really, for a chance to win our SAY CHEERS! SHOW US YOUR SIPS! event_description: A protected and paved 51.7-mile, multi-use Trail connecting Richmond and Williamsburg along the beautiful and historic Route 5 corridor and James River, the Virginia Capital Trail is a gem of a resource for runners and walkers. Choose your race: Half Marathon 10-Mile Feed More 5K Mummy Mile for runners 12 & under Then grab your friends and get ready for race-day fun! Party pacers, cheer stations, top-finisher prizes by Lucky Road, a finish-line party, awards ceremony, medals, event shirts, costume contests, and plenty of energy from charity partner, We Off the Couch! event_name: Free Salsa at the Valentine Museum
event_description: Salsa can feel intimidating from the sidelines. If you have ever hesitated to join the dance floor, here is your sign: you can absolutely learn to dance! Join Mambo Bones Salsa Dance Studio at The Valentine Museum for an hour of rhythm, connection, and energy. We teach the basics of salsa and bachata from the ground up in a low-pressure, friendly environment where everyone is welcome. What to Expect Zero Experience Required: If you can walk, you can dance. We break everything down into easy, manageable steps. Come Solo or With a Partner: You do not need a partner to join. We rotate during class, making it the perfect way to meet new people. One Hour of Joy: We pack plenty of energy into a single hour. It is the perfect mid-week mood-booster. Good Vibes Only: Our class is judgment-free. Wear comfortable clothes and shoes you can move in, bring your energy, and let’s get moving. Event Details Who: Taught by the instructors at Mambo Bones Salsa Dance Studio. Where: The Valentine Museum. Duration: 1 hour. Bring: Just yourself, some water, and an open mind. What to Wear: If shoes have too much grip (like most running sneakers or hiking boots), your feet get stuck during turns, which puts a lot of stress on your ankles and knees. For the Ladies: Smooth-soled flats: Think loafers or dress shoes with a hard plastic or leather sole. Low, sturdy heels: If you want some height, choose a block heel or a wedge with an ankle strap. Avoid stilettos or "slip-on" heels that might fly off mid-turn. Dance Sneakers: Brands like Fuegos are popular because they look like street shoes but are designed to spin. For the Gentlemen: Dress shoes: Leather-soled oxfords or loafers are perfect because they slide easily. Minimalist Sneakers: Look for shoes with a worn-down, flatter tread rather than deep, "toothy" grips. Overall rule of thumb for shoes: Wear something comfortable that stays securely on the foot and has a relatively smooth bottom. If you can pivot on the ball of your foot on a kitchen floor without getting stuck, you are good to go! Where Should I Park? Free parking is available in the Adult Outpatient Pavilion (AOP) Visitor Parking Deck (one block from the Valentine) at 1001 E. Leigh Street. The self-parking entrance is located on N. 11th Street. Please take the elevator to Ground Level (GL) to exit the building onto Leigh Street. You will need to bring the parking ticket with you to the front desk at the Valentine to validate your parking before leaving the Valentine at the conclusion of your visit. Paid street parking is also available. For more information, see the Parking Lot Rules and Regulations section of our Museum and Visitor Policies. Additionally, there is a small parking lot behind the museum at 407 N. 10th Street. Parking is very limited in this lot, and there will not be a parking attendant. The Valentine is located two blocks east of the Downtown Transfer Station, which services numerous GRTC Bus Routes. If taking the GRTC Pulse, disembark at the Government Center station at Broad & 9th Street for easy access to the Valentine. If you would benefit from wheelchair accessible parking or have any questions about visiting and accessibility, please call our front desk at (804) 649-0711 ext. 301 and we will be happy to assist you. Ready to dance? Spaces go fast, so grab your spot today!

event_name: Fall Concert Series: Alan Biller x Sara Bouchard
event_description: Sara Bouchard is a multidisciplinary artist and composer who uses sound, installation, works on paper, performance and creative coding to interweave song, history and the landscape. She is currently based in Richmond, VA, where she teaches at Virginia Commonwealth University School of the Arts. Guitarist Alan Biller has lived and performed in NYC, Montreal, Washington DC, and Richmond, VA as part of their lively jazz scenes. He has performed worldwide with the Capital Focus Jazz Band, playing at the French Quarter Festival in New Orleans, the Old Sacramento Dixieland Jazz Jubilee, and the Ascona Jazz Festival in Ascona, Switzerland. He also spent several months performing on Carnival Cruise Lines and lived to tell about it. He has studied with such famous (and infamous) jazz greats as Bruce Arnold, Mordy Ferber, Ron McClure, Frank Kimbrough, and George Garzone. He received his BMus from NYU. With his solo project Wolf In Wool, he tries to make his guitar sound like anything but a guitar, with varying levels of success.

event_name: Claimed by the Orc King with Roxy Taylor
event_description: Calling all monster romance lovers! We are thrilled to have Roxy Taylor coming by to talk about her fantastical and sexy debut, Claimed By The Orc King . She will be discussing all things romantasy with Fountain Fave Author Sara Raasch! About the Book: A fated mates monster romance featuring an orc king, a portal to a brutal fantasy realm, and a heroine who refuses to kneel. This beautiful trade paperback edition features a deluxe jacket with silver foil on the front and a full-color interior illustration. Thena came to FantastiCon to survive the weekend with minimal human interaction and maximum sarcasm. She didn’t plan on catching the attention of a seven-foot orc painted in war green—or the way her pulse stutters when he looks at her like she’s already his. Viggo Klausson isn’t a cosplayer. He’s the High Chieftain of the Eastern Orcs, stranded in the human world while searching for the mate fate promised him. The moment he scents Thena, the bond snaps tight. Then a portal drags her into Korule—a fractured kingdom where women are rare, power is carved in blood, and claiming a mate can start a war. Thena refuses to become anyone’s prize. An ancient magic awakens inside her, and suddenly she’s not just the king’s fated mate. She’s dangerous. Viggo may be steady. He may be patient. But when enemies circle, he does not hesitate to bare his teeth. He found his mate. Now he has to earn her. Perfect for readers who love: • Fated mates • Orc kings • Strong, sharp-tongued heroines • Political court intrigue • Portal fantasy romance • “Touch her and die” energy About the Author: Roxy Taylor is a GenX Amazon writing romantasy that refuses to behave. She writes about women who never fold themselves smaller, and the men or monsters caught between worshiping them and surviving them. Fueled by a lifelong love of ‘80s films, she writes for women who remember adventure and refuse to settle for less. About the Moderator: Sara Raasch has known she was destined for bookish things since the age of five, when her friends had a lemonade stand and she tagged along to sell her hand-drawn picture books too. Not much has changed since then — her friends still cock concerned eyebrows when she attempts to draw things and her enthusiasm for the written word still drives her to extreme measures. She is the New York Times and USA Today bestselling author of multiple books for teens, including the historical romantasy duology WITCH AND HUNTER, cowritten with Beth Revis; as well as romances for adults, such as THE NIGHTMARE BEFORE KISSMAS and THE ENTANGLEMENT OF RIVAL WIZARDS. ​​None of her books feature her hand-drawn pictures. Withfriends believes in building financial resilience for indie bookstores through community support.

event_name: Lecture | Land, Liberty and Loyalties: Virginia Indian Participation in the Revolutionary War
event_description: Join us for a free lecture presented by anthropologist Ashley Spivey, Ph.D., and historian Katie Gibson, M.A., about the individual choices tribal citizens made in aims to protect their land, defend their liberty and question their loyalties during the Revolutionary War. Spivey and Gibson will explore the complex choices Indigenous peoples in Virginia faced during the Revolutionary War and how these decisions shaped their communities. They will examine treaty relationships and political alliances of Virginia tribes in the 18th century and analyze why some supported the Patriots while others sided with the British or remained neutral. The talk will also consider the war’s aftermath, including land bounties granted to Indigenous veterans and pension claims by widows. Examples of Pamunkey participation in the war include the stories of Brafferton Indian School students Robert Mush and George Sampson, and John Collins and his wife, Jane, who served on the front lines. These narratives reveal how tribal citizens navigated loyalty, liberty and survival amid profound social and political pressures. Spivey is an historical anthropologist specializing in the archaeology and culture of Powhatan Algonquian communities located in Tidewater Virginia. Her academic and professional experience has centered on supporting tribal sovereignty through tribal cultural and natural resource management and tribal historic preservation. She has worked with tribes, universities, museums and federal and state agencies to support and implement historic preservation as well as cultural and natural resource management programs that incorporate the needs of tribal communities. As a member of the Pamunkey Indian Tribe, Spivey has a close connection to the Indigenous communities of Virginia, including developing Indigenous-led cultural heritage and natural resource management strategies and facilitating administrative capacity building through consultation on program development and implementation. Gibson is a public historian with experience in research, archives, genealogy and federal acknowledgment. She has worked in different capacities with her local historical organizations and is interested in the historic preservations of underrepresented histories. She has previously worked as an archive and collections specialist with the Mattaponi Indian Reservation on their petition for federal acknowledgement. This event is part of the Library’s programming commemorating Virginia's role in the 250th anniversary of American independence. This event is free, but registration is required. Limited free parking is available underneath the Library at 800 East Broad Street. For more information, contact education@lva.virginia.gov.

event_name: Free Intro Salsa and Bachata Dance Lessons
event_description: Salsa can feel intimidating from the sidelines. If you have ever hesitated to join the dance floor, here is your sign: you can absolutely learn to dance! Join Mambo Bones Salsa Dance Studio at The Valentine Museum for an hour of rhythm, connection, and energy. We teach the basics of salsa and bachata from the ground up in a low-pressure, friendly environment where everyone is welcome. What to Expect Zero Experience Required: If you can walk, you can dance. We break everything down into easy, manageable steps. Come Solo or With a Partner: You do not need a partner to join. We rotate during class, making it the perfect way to meet new people. One Hour of Joy: We pack plenty of energy into a single hour. It is the perfect mid-week mood-booster. This event is free, but registration is required.
